exposure: Care funded by the Department of Defence
outcome: Mode of delivery (Caesarean section, non-instrumental vaginal birth)
Out-of-pocket costs for birth and healthcare in the first two years of life
cohort: Women giving birth between July 1, 2012, and June 30, 2018, in Queensland, Australia (n = 365,138 births), including 395 women serving in the Australian Defence Force at the time of birth.
finding: Compared to a matched civilian sample, Australian Defence Force servicewomen had higher odds of caesarean section and epidural use, lower odds of non-instrumental vaginal birth, and significantly higher out-of-pocket healthcare costs for their children up to two years of age.
mod_finding: Australian Defence Force servicewomen had significantly greater odds of having a caesarean section and epidural, and significantly lower odds of having a non-instrumental vaginal birth compared to a matched civilian population.
